# iliad-053 (9.114–204) — new renderings

Rows are in the format of the conventions table: Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose.

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπεν ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων (9.114, whole-line reply-formula with αὖτε) | "Him then in turn addressed the lord of men, Agamemnon:" | "Then Agamemnon, lord of men, spoke to him in turn:" | "answered" (reserved for ἠμείβετο); built on the table's τὸν δ’ αὖτε προσέειπε and ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Ἀγαμέμνων |
| ἄτη · ἀασάμην (ἐμὰς ἄτας 9.115; ἀασάμην 9.116, 9.119) | "my bewilderments" · "I was bewildered" | "my bewilderments" · "I was bewildered" | "blind folly" (turned down in the Odyssey table), "ruin" (shipped at 12.372, a different use), "I was blinded" (the Odyssey's rendering of ἀάσθη, 4.503, kept for that tense); the noun and verb are kept as one family so that the echo of 115–116 is heard, as in the Odyssey's ἀάω · ἄτη (21.296–302); the plural noun is "bewilderments", the separate occasions |
| οὔ τι ψεῦδος … κατέλεξας (9.115) | "not at all a falsehood … have you recounted" | "you have recounted … and not falsely" | "you have not lied" (loses καταλέγω "recount"); ψεῦδος used like an adverb is the usual explanation, and the note says so |
| λευγαλέῃσι φρεσί (9.119) | "pitiful wits" | "my pitiful wits" | "wretched" (reserved for δύστηνος), "feeble"; follows the Odyssey's λευγαλέος "pitiful" (5.312, 16.273), φρήν "wits" |
| πιθήσας (φρεσὶ πιθήσας, 9.119) | "having obeyed" | "gave way to" | "yielded" (kept for εἴξας, 9.109), "trusted"; πιθέω is "obey", the epic form beside πείθομαι |
| ἂψ ἐθέλω ἀρέσαι (9.120) | "back I wish to make him content" | "I wish, in return, to make him content" | "please", "appease"; keeps 9.112's "make him content" (ἀρεσσάμενοι); the Greek has no object and the note says "him" is Achilles |
| ἀπύρους τρίποδας (9.122) | "unfired tripods" | "unfired tripods" | "untouched by fire" (a gloss), "new", "never used"; ἄπυρος "without fire", τρίπους "tripod" (the Odyssey's λοετροχόος τρίπους) |
| αἴθωνας λέβητας (9.123) | "fire-bright cauldrons" | "fire-bright cauldrons" | "gleaming", "tawny"; follows the table's αἴθων "fire-bright" and λέβης "cauldron" (Odyssey 15.84) |
| πηγούς ἀθλοφόρους (ἵππους, 9.124) | "strong-packed, prize-bearing" | "sturdy, prize-bearing" (+ note: πηγός from πήγνυμι "make firm", sense not certain) | "strong" alone, "prize-winning" (kept for the verb ἄροντο), "swift"; πηγός follows the Odyssey's κύματι πηγῷ "strong-packed wave" in `l`, with "sturdy" in `i` for a living creature |
| ἀέθλια … ἄροντο / ἠνείκαντο (9.124, 9.127) | "contest-prizes … won" / "carried off" | "prizes in contests … won" / "have won me in prizes" | "trophies", "games" (reserved for the ἄεθλον "contest" sense in the Odyssey table); ἀέθλια keeps "contest-prizes" (Odyssey 21.62), ἄρνυμαι "win" |
| ἀλήϊος (9.125) | "without a field of grain" | "without a field of grain" | "landless", "poor", "without a farm"; ἀ- + λήϊον "standing crop" |
| ἐρίτιμοιο χρυσοῖο (9.126) | "of much-honoured gold" | "much-honoured gold" | "precious gold", "costly" (turned down for ἐρίτιμον at 2.447); ἐρι- an intensifier |
| ἐϋκτιμένην Λέσβον (9.129) | "well-built Lesbos" | "well-settled Lesbos" | "well-founded", "stately"; follows the Odyssey's ἐυκτιμένην νῆσον (9.130) "the island well-built" / "a well-settled place" |
| κάλλει ἐνίκων (9.130) | "in beauty surpassed" | "surpassed … in beauty" | "outdid", "were victors"; νικάω with an accusative of persons is "surpass" (2.370) |
| ἐπιβήμεναι εὐνῆς · μιγῆναι (9.133) | "to have set foot upon her bed" · "to have mingled with her" | "went up to her bed" · "lay with her" | "mounted", "made love"; εὐνή keeps "bed" (Odyssey 10.297 ff, the intimate bed), ἐπιβαίνω "set foot on", μίγνυμι "mingle" (Odyssey 5.126) |
| ἣ θέμις ἀνθρώπων πέλει (9.134) | "as is the custom of human beings" | "as is the custom of human beings, men and women" | "law", "right" (reserved for other words); θέμις keeps "custom" (2.73) |
| νῆα ἅλις χρυσοῦ καὶ χαλκοῦ νηησάσθω (9.137, νηέω aorist middle imperative; ἅλις with a genitive) | "a ship with plenty of gold and bronze let him load for himself" | "let him go in and load a ship with plenty of gold and bronze" | "heap", "fill" alone, "enough"; νηέω is "heap up, load", ἅλις "plenty" |
| οὖθαρ ἀρούρης (9.141) | "the udder of the plough-land" | "the udder of the plough-land" | "the rich plough-land", "the fat of the land" (drop the image); ἄρουρα keeps the Odyssey's "plough-land", and the note says the udder is a figure for richness |
| τηλύγετος (Ὀρέστῃ, 9.143) | "late-born" | "late-born" | "darling", "cherished"; keeps the shipped "late-born" (iliad-018, -028; odyssey-014, -077) |
| θαλίῃ ἔνι πολλῇ (9.143) | "in much abundance" | "in great abundance" | "in luxury", "with every comfort"; θαλίη is "plenty, festive abundance", related to the table's δαὶς θάλεια "abundant feast" |
| ἀνάεδνον (9.146) | "without bridal gifts" | "without bridal gifts" | "unwooed", "without a bride-price", "for nothing"; ἕδνα keeps "bridal gifts" (Odyssey 19.529 ff) |
| μείλια (9.147) | "dowry-gifts" | "a dowry" (+ note: root of μειλίσσω "soothe"; sense usual, not certain) | "soothing gifts", "settlement", "bride-gifts" (reserved for ἕδνα); gifts given by the bride's father with her |
| εὖ ναιόμενα πτολίεθρα (9.149) | "well-inhabited citadels" | "well-inhabited citadels" | "well-built towns" (taken by ἐϋκτίμενος), "cities" (reserved for πόλις); πτολίεθρον keeps "citadel" (Odyssey 3.4), ναίω "dwell" (Odyssey 17.28) |
| ποιήεσσαν · βαθύλειμον (9.150–151, epithets of towns) | "grassy" · "deep-meadowed" | "grassy" · "deep-meadowed" | "grassy-meadowed", "meadow-rich", "of the deep grass"; βαθύς "deep", λειμών "meadow" |
| νέαται Πύλου (9.153) | "the furthest of sandy Pylos" | "at the farthest edge of sandy Pylos" (+ note: sense from the word) | "on the borders of", "the last of Pylos" |
| πολύρρηνες πολυβοῦται (9.154) | "rich in sheep, rich in cattle" | "rich in sheep and rich in cattle" | "rich in flocks and herds" (loses the "sheep"/"cattle" pair); follows the Odyssey's πολύρρηνος "rich in sheep" (11.257) |
| λιπαρὰς θέμιστας (9.156) | "sleek rules of right" | "sleek rules of right" (+ note: dues paid to a king, sense not certain) | "rich tribute", "fat dues", "just judgments" (each picks one reading); λιπαρός keeps "sleek" (Odyssey 19.368), θέμιστες "rules of right" (Odyssey 9.112) |
| δμηθήτω · ἀδάμαστος (9.158) | "Let him be subdued" · "unsubdued" | "Let him be subdued" · "unsubdued" | "tamed", "conquered", "unconquerable", "unyielding"; both come from δαμάζω, which keeps "subdue" (5.106), and the echo of δμηθήτω in ἀδάμαστος is the point |
| ἀμείλιχος (9.158) | "ungentle" | "unrelenting" | "implacable", "pitiless"; ἀ- + the root of μειλίσσω "soothe"; kept apart from the table's μειλίχιος "gentle" |
| ὑποστήτω (9.160) | "let him submit" | "let him submit" | "obey", "bow", "yield" (kept for πιθέσθων, εἴκω); ὑφίστημι in its intransitive sense "stand under" |
| βασιλεύτερος · προγενέστερος (9.160–161) | "more kingly" · "the elder" | "the more kingly" · "the elder in age" | "greater king", "older in years"; βασιλεύτερος keeps the shipped βασιλεύτατος "the most kingly" (9.69), γενεῇ "in birth, in age" (7.153) |
| εὔχομαι εἶναι (9.161) | "I claim to be" | "I claim to be" | "I pray", "I boast" (reserved for other words); follows the table's εὔχεται εἶναι (2.82) and 3.430–431 |
| ὀνοστά (9.164) | "no longer to be found fault with" | "that can no longer be found fault with" | "not to be scorned", "not to be despised" (kept for ἀπόβλητα, 3.65), "to be refused"; ὀνοστός from ὄνομαι "find fault with, disdain" |
| κλητούς (9.165) | "summoned men" | "chosen men" | "called men", "invited men" (reserved for the Odyssey's κλητός, 17.386), "envoys" (names what the Greek leaves unsaid); follows the table's πολύκλητοι "many-summoned" |
| τοὺς ἂν ἐγὼ ἐπιόψομαι (9.167) | "those whom I shall look over" | "those whom I shall pick out" | "choose" in `l`, "inspect", "select"; ἐφοράω "look upon", the gap in the Greek (no main verb) left as it is |
| φέρτε δὲ χερσὶν ὕδωρ, εὐφημῆσαί τε κέλεσθε (9.171) | "and bring water for the hands, and bid them keep holy silence" | "and bring water for our hands, and bid them keep a holy silence" | "command silence", "call for quiet" (drop the sacral sense of εὐφημέω); χερσίν "for the hands" (to wash), κέλομαι "bid" |
| Διὶ Κρονίδῃ ἀρησόμεθ’, αἴ κ’ ἐλεήσῃ (9.172) | "to Zeus, the son-of-Cronus, we may pray, if he may take pity" | "we may pray to Zeus, son of Cronus, in case he takes pity" | "if he will have mercy", "perhaps he will pity us"; Κρονίδης "son of Cronus" (the Odyssey table), ἐλεέω "take pity" |
| ὣς φάτο, τοῖσι δὲ πᾶσιν ἑαδότα μῦθον ἔειπεν (9.173, whole line; reused from Odyssey 18.422, which has ἔειπε) | "So he spoke, and to them all a pleasing speech he uttered." | "So he spoke, and what he said pleased them all." | the Odyssey's wording, unchanged; "a speech they all approved", "welcome" |
| δενδίλλων (9.180; rare, sense not known) | "casting glances" | "casting glances" (+ note: usual explanation "meaningful glances", exact sense not known) | "nodding", "winking", "signalling" (each decides the guess) |
| εὐχομένω (dual participle, with a dative of a god, 9.183) | "praying" | "praying" | "boasting", "declaring"; εὔχομαι takes the table's "praying" where a god is the addressee (1.43), "declare" in the Odyssey table where a status is claimed, "claim" with an infinitive |
| γαιηόχῳ ἐννοσιγαίῳ (9.183, of Poseidon, unnamed) | "the earth-holder, the earth-shaker" | "the earth-holder, the earth-shaker" | "Poseidon" (the Greek withholds the name); the two epithets are fixed in the table (γαιήοχος, ἐννοσίγαιος) and together they follow the Odyssey's γαιήοχος ἐννοσίγαιος (11.241) |
| ῥηϊδίως πεπιθεῖν μεγάλας φρένας Αἰακίδαο (9.184) | "easily to persuade the great wits of the descendant of Aeacus" | "that they might easily persuade the great mind of the descendant of Aeacus" | "the proud heart", "the stubborn mind" (each reads μεγάλας); Αἰακίδης keeps "descendant of Aeacus" (2.860) |
| λιγείῃ φόρμιγγι (9.186) | "a clear lyre" | "a clear-sounding lyre" | "clear-toned" (turned down for the heralds), "shrill", "sweet-toned"; λιγύς keeps "clear" (1.248); φόρμιγξ "lyre" |
| ἀργύρεον ζυγόν (9.187) | "a silver yoke" | "a silver cross-bar" | "silver bridge", "silver frame", "silver crossbeam"; ζυγόν keeps "yoke" in `l` as at 2.293, and `i` says what a yoke is on a lyre |
| ἐξ ἐνάρων (9.188) | "from the spoils" | "from the spoils" | "spoils of war", "booty" (reserved for ληΐς "spoil" in the Odyssey table); ἔναρα "spoils stripped from the slain" (5.155) |
| ταφών (9.193) | "amazed" | "in amazement" (+ note: aorist participle of the verb of τέθηπα and τάφος) | "stunned", "struck dumb"; keeps "amazement" for τάφος and "was struck with wonder" for θάμβησεν |
| δεικνύμενος προσέφη (9.196; sense uncertain, the lexicons' "greeting by gesture") | "greeting by gesture" | "greeting the two with a gesture" (+ note: the sense is the lexicons', not certain) | "pointing out", "showing them in", "welcoming" alone; the sense of δείκνυμι is "show" |
| χαίρετον (9.197, dual, greeting on meeting) | "Welcome, you two" | "Welcome, you two" | "Hail", "Greetings" (kept apart from the table's χαῖρε, ξεῖνε "Welcome, stranger"), "rejoice"; follows χαίρετε κήρυκες "Welcome, heralds" (1.334) with the dual |
| σκυζομένῳ περ (9.198) | "though I am sullen" | "though I am sullen" | "angry" (reserved for χόλος), "although I am wrathful"; follows the table's σκυζομένη "sullen" (4.23) |
| κλισμοῖσι τάπησί τε πορφυρέοισιν (9.200) | "on seats and on purple rugs" | "on seats and on purple rugs" | "reclining chairs", "purple coverlets", "carpets"; κλισμός keeps "seat" (Odyssey 17.86), πορφύρεος "purple" (3.126) |
| ζωρότερον κέραιε (9.203; ζωρός "strong", sense not certain) | "stronger mix it" | "mix it stronger" | "warmer", "hotter" (the other ancient guess, named in the note), "pour it purer"; κεραίω "mix" (4.260, κέρωνται "mix") |
| ἐμῷ ὑπέασι μελάθρῳ (9.204) | "under my roof" | "under my roof" | "rafter" (the Odyssey table's single beam, 22.239), "palace" (the table's Priam's roof, 2.414), "hut"; μέλαθρον "roof" here stands for the hut |
| names of the towns (9.150–152) and the daughters (9.145) | Cardamyle, Enope, Hire, Pherae, Antheia, Aepeia, Pedasus; Chrysothemis, Laodice, Iphianassa | same | Latinised forms as the other Iliad names ("Cardamyle" not "Kardamyle"); Ἱρή "Hire", Φηραί "Pherae" |

Departures from the Odyssey: none. The Odyssey's wording is kept where it was fixed (Odyssey 1.148, 1.146 for the heralds' line, 3.340–342 and 7.184 for the libation line, 18.422 for ὣς φάτο … ἑαδότα μῦθον ἔειπεν); the Iliad's own lines (9.162 = 4.317, 9.163 = 2.434, 9.176 = 1.471, 9.185 = 1.328) take the English already shipped.
